children: Skyways Air Services shares are expected to make their market debut at a premium of around 22-26 percent over the IPO price on September 1, an analyst said.
The company's shares are scheduled to list on Tuesday, after its Rs 582.79-crore initial public offering was subscribed 71.25 times. The IPO had a price band of Rs 131-138 per share.

Mahesh M Ojha, Vice President, Research & Business Development at Kantilal Chhaganlal Securities, said the company has a strong position in air freight forwarding, a growing domestic and international network and technology-led efficiency initiatives.

He said the company could benefit from the expansion of India's air cargo and supply-chain infrastructure, offering a long-term growth opportunity. However, near-term profitability remains sensitive to industry cycles.
"We expect the listing gain of 22-26 percent. For IPO allottees, short-term investors can book profit, while long-term investors can hold the shares," Ojha said.

Skyways Air Services is an air freight forwarding and logistics company with a presence across 28 locations in India and international operations across key global trade hubs. The company has maintained the No. 1 position in air freight forwarding by AWB generation for the past four calendar years, supported by relationships with leading global airlines and a logistics partner network.

The company is also expanding its capabilities through technology platforms such as SLS HIKE and SLS 100X. Its consortium with Swissport International AG for the proposed Kolkata cargo terminal provides an additional long-term growth opportunity.
However, the company reported thin PAT margins of around 2.26 percent in FY26, making profitability sensitive to air cargo rates, fuel surcharges and global trade volumes, Ojha added.
The business remains exposed to freight rate volatility, dependence on third-party carriers and working capital-intensive operations.

At the upper end of the price band, the issue is valued at 31.6 times FY26 annualised earnings and 19.8 times EV/EBITDA. This implies a post-issue market capitalisation of Rs 20,057 million, making the issue fully priced.

Narendra Solanki, Head-Fundamental Research-Investment Services at Anand Rathi Shares and Stock Brokers, said investors who receive allotment may consider booking partial profits after listing and holding the remaining shares for the long term, considering the company's strong market position, diversified service portfolio and favourable industry outlook.
